value.notes: War on nobody. Trust: .

Shechem is a small vassal of Egypt (tribute 10 a year; I serve Egypt and send troops when called). Treasury 33, army 300 men in Shechem. Megiddo's army was destroyed; Gezer's army now stands inside Megiddo's walls. Envoy Piyama-Kurunta (c72) is on his way to Megiddo to seal a peace of brotherhood (no troops into each other's lands). Keep the army at home, spend little, watch Gezer and Aijalon. Avoid breaking the vassal oath to Egypt.
value.summary: Turn 2. Small vassal of Egypt in a hill land (Shechem). Army of 300 at home. Envoy en route to Megiddo for a non-aggression brotherhood tablet. Holding position; economy minimal.

ledger.entry: Vassal by sealed tablet (turn 0): tribute 10 shekels a year; I serve Egypt and send troops when called. Nothing paid yet this year; I keep my oath.
Envoy Piyama-Kurunta sent turn 1 to propose peace and brotherhood, no troops into each other's lands, tablet to seal. Awaiting reply.

value.notes: Turn 2. Pella is small: one 500-man army, 36 shekels, 40 grain, 9 tax a season. Vassal of Egypt (tribute 5/yr owed, tablet k57). Gezer's army now sits in Megiddo after destroying Megiddo's army. Gezer and Megiddo are Egyptian vassals too; let Egypt judge that quarrel. Hold at home, keep troops paid and fed, avoid war. Tribute to Egypt not yet sent; send when treasury allows, by envoy (scribe fee 20). Watch Hazor and Ashtaroth.
value.summary: Turn 1-2: Pella holds with its 500-man army at home. Vassal of Egypt. No diplomacy yet. Gezer defeated Megiddo's army and is inside Megiddo's walls; watching.

ledger.entry: Vassal of Egypt by sealed tablet (turn 0, copy k57): tribute 5 shekels a year; we serve Egypt and Egypt protects our land. No tribute sent yet; to send when gold allows.

value.notes: Jerusalem is a tiny vassal of Egypt (tribute 5 shekels a year, tablet k21). Treasury 9. Army of 100 in Jerusalem holds. Keep the peace, pay tribute through Shuttiya (c84), and avoid any war with neighbours (Gath, Aijalon, Pella, Shechem are other powers' troops or small holdings). Watch Egypt's word and any move against my land; the standing order to pay and feed troops stays. Build nothing until gold allows.
value.summary: Turn 2, first orders. Vassal of Egypt; tribute 5 shekels a year sent by envoy Shuttiya (c84, arriving about turn 3). Holding Jerusalem with 100 men. No war planned.

ledger.entry: Vassal of Egypt by sealed tablet (k21, turn 0): tribute 5 shekels of gold a year; I take no arms against Egypt or its friends and my troops come when called; Egypt guards my land. Turn 1: envoy Shuttiya sent with 5 shekels as this year's tribute and a message of loyalty.

value.notes: Lakisha is a small vassal of Egypt (tablet k31: 5 shekels tribute a year, I serve Egypt, Egypt protects my land). Neighbours: Ashkelon (500 men), Gath (500), Shasu (2500 desert army, dangerous), Gezer and Aijalon beyond. Treasury is only 11 shekels. Priorities: keep the army at home, keep the tribute paid to Egypt, avoid any war, grow the grain stores and the tax base. Do not spend gold abroad except tribute. Watch Shasu and Gath for any move against Lachish.
value.summary: Turn 2: first orders. Holding Lakisha quietly. Envoy Ilu-shalim (c71) carries the year's 5-shekel tribute to Egypt. Army at Lachish holds. Keep the realm intact and loyal to Egypt.

ledger.entry: Vassal by sealed tablet (k31, turn 0): 5 shekels of gold a year as tribute; I serve Egypt and take no arms against it or its friends; Egypt protects my land. Turn 1: Ilu-shalim (c71) sent with 5 shekels tribute, due about turn 3. Nothing broken.

value.notes: Tunip is a small vassal of Egypt (tribute 10 shekels a year, sealed turn 0). Treasury about 24 shekels; troops cost 3 a season. Priorities: keep the city and army alive, pay tribute, avoid wars with neighbours (Ugarit, Niya, Qatna, Amurru), and let the treasury and people grow. Envoy Abdi-Baalu (c99) carries the tribute to Egypt; he is due back about turn 3 and his job pays 60 more on completion. Watch for foreign troops; the army in Tunip holds. Revisit when envoys return or troops appear.
value.summary: Turn 2: first orders. Holding Tunip with its army; tribute to Egypt on the road via Abdi-Baalu; no construction; no new policy. Egypt is overlord; Ugarit, Niya, Qatna, Amurru are the neighbours with troops nearby.

ledger.entry: Vassal to Egypt by sealed tablet (turn 0): 10 shekels of tribute a year. Turn 1: envoy Abdi-Baalu sent with 10 shekels as this year's tribute, mandate to deliver it and promise nothing more. Envoy's job pays 120 total (60 on hand, 60 when done by turn 13).

value.notes: Turn 2. Upe (Damascus), Egyptian vassal paying 10 shekels tribute a year via Arzawiya (c64, on the road to Egypt, due back about turn 3). Army of 750 in Damascus is my only force; it holds. Neighbours: Qadesh (strong walls 3, Egypt's vassal too), Byblos, Beirut, Sidon (Egypt's vassals), Hazor and Ashtaroth (small, walled). Hatti and Mitanni are far. Plan: stay quiet, keep the tribute, keep the army at home, grow the land and stores, watch for a neighbour looking away. Do not spend gold on fees unless needed. Teuwatti (c65) is at my court, free, asks 16 a season; no job for now.
value.summary: Season 2. Vassal of Egypt (tablet k13, tribute 10 a year). Holding Damascus with 750 men. Envoy c64 carrying the tribute to Egypt. No other dealings yet.

ledger.entry: Vassal of Egypt by tablet k13 (turn 0): 10 shekels tribute a year, sent by envoy Arzawiya (c64) with 10 shekels, turn 1. Promised nothing more. Paid so far.

value.notes: Hazor is small: walls 3, one army of 500, 11 shekels. Egypt is my overlord (tribute 5/yr via Yadinu). Plan: hold the walls, keep the army fed and paid, grow the people and grain, avoid wars with neighbours (Damascus 750, Akko 500, Sidon 500, Pella/Ashtaroth 500). Watch Egypt's word and any move toward Hazor. Do not spend gold beyond tribute.
value.summary: Turn 2. Hazor, vassal of Egypt. Holding. Army of 500 in Hazor on hold. Yadinu en route to Egypt with tribute. No schedule yet.

ledger.entry: Vassal of Egypt by sealed tablet (turn 0): 5 shekels tribute a year, no arms against Egypt or its friends, troops to come when called, Egypt protects our land. Turn 1: Yadinu sent with 5 shekels tribute, mandate: deliver tribute, promise nothing more.

value.notes: Arwad is a small coastal city with one fleet (in Sumur/Arwad waters, now trading at Delta). Few shekels (about 33). Plan: survive, stay out of wars, grow by grain trade and the harbour. Envoys Maya (to Hatti) and Puzru (to Egypt) carry proposals of brotherhood and peace with a sealed oath of no troops across borders. Do not spend gold we lack. Watch Sidon, Byblos, Amurru and Tyre (neighbours) for threats; the fleet protects our waters. When envoys return, reopen orders and read their reports.
value.summary: Turn 2. First orders. Arwad: walls 2, harbour 2, 2k fighting men, tax 38%. Envoys Maya (Hatti) and Puzru (Egypt) away proposing brotherhood and peace. No land neighbours; sea-bound. Strategy: peace, trade, keep walls and harbour, avoid costly wars.

ledger.entry: Turn 1: Puzru sent to propose brotherhood and a sealed oath of no troops across each other's lands (tablet by Shamash, Amun, Marduk, Teshub). Outcome pending.
Turn 1: Maya sent to propose brotherhood and a sealed oath of no troops across each other's lands. Outcome pending.

value.notes: Turn 2. Amurru is small: 17 shekels, one army of 1250 men, 1k fighting men. Egypt is my overlord by vassal tablet (10 shekels tribute a year); Milku-ahi carries this year's tribute. Pu-Baalu is offering the Suteans vassalage for 5 shekels a year, with my troops guarding their land. Plan: hold, keep the army at home, pay troops, and watch neighbours (Qatna, Qadesh, Tunip, Byblos, Sumur) for a chance. Do not spend gold we cannot spare. Watch Egypt's answer on the tribute and whether Egypt's troops at Sumur move.
value.summary: Opening. Holding Amurru with its army. Egypt is overlord (vassal since turn 0). Envoys out: Milku-ahi to Egypt with tribute, Pu-Baalu to the Suteans. Treasury is very thin.

ledger.entry: Vassal by sealed tablet (turn 0): 10 shekels tribute a year. Turn 1: Milku-ahi sent to Egypt with 10 shekels tribute for this year, mandate: deliver, promise nothing more.
Turn 1: Pu-Baalu sent to offer vassalage (Suteans pay 5 shekels a year, my troops guard their land). Tablet to seal; no land or gold promised beyond that.

value.notes: Nuhashshe is a small vassal of Mitanni (10 shekels tribute a year, sealed turn 0, copy k43). Army of 1000 men at home is our only real defence; keep it at home, avoid battle, keep the people fed. Alalakh (brother, peace pact tablet being carried by c88) is our only friendly neighbour; Niya, Qatna, Aleppo and the Suteans border us. Watch Mitanni's answer on tribute and whether Alalakh seals the no-troops pact. Grow the treasury; do not waste gold. Do not wake for small matters.
value.summary: Turn 2. Small vassal kingdom of Nuhashshe (Mitanni's vassal). Envoys out: c111 to Mitanni (tribute 10 shekels, mandate deliver and promise nothing more); c88 to Alalakh (peace and no-troops pact tablet). Army of 1000 holds at Nuhashshe. Tax 37%. Treasury 18.

ledger.entry: Vassal to Mitanni by tablet of turn 0 (k43): 10 shekels tribute a year, protection and service when called. Tribute carried by c111 in turn 1 (10 shekels). Not yet answered.
Sent c88 in turn 1 with a proposed tablet: brotherhood, neither king sends troops into the other's land. Awaiting answer.

value.notes: Gath is tiny: treasury ~11, one army of 500 at gath, 1k fighting men, vassal of Egypt (tribute 5/yr, carried by Yarimanu c90, due back ~turn 3). Plan: stay quiet, hold the capital, keep taxes and pay as they are, keep the army at home. Egypt is the overlord; keep the vassal tribute paid on time to protect name. Watch Hatti/Assyria/Babylonia and the Gezer/Megiddo fighting to the north; do not provoke. Build treasury before any spending.
value.summary: Turn 2. Gath (Gimti), Shuwardata. Egypt's vassal (5 shekels/yr tribute). Army 500 at gath, walls 1, police 50. Tax 37%. Treasury 11. Envoy Yarimanu (c90) travelling to Egypt with tribute; due back turn 3. No conflicts. Strategy: hold, grow treasury and grain, stay loyal to Egypt, avoid wars.

ledger.entry: Vassal of Egypt by sealed tablet (turn 0): 5 shekels tribute a year. Turn 1: sent Yarimanu (c90) with 5 shekels as this year's tribute, mandate deliver only. Promised nothing more.

value.notes: Niya is a small vassal of Mitanni (tablet k61: 10 shekels tribute a year, protection clause, our troops answer Mitanni's call). Treasury is only 21 shekels, and troops cost 3 a season, so keep the army at home and the tax as it is. Envoy c57 (Akit-Teshup) is Takuwa's own brother and once turned Niya against him: watch him, and do not give him more gold or tablets than the tribute. Priorities: keep the army paid and fed, collect the caravan's 22 shekels, pay the tribute yearly through Akit-Teshup or a fresh envoy, and stay out of wars. Watch Mitanni's strength and whether Hatti or Babylonia pressure Niya's roads (Alalakh, Ugarit, Nuhashshe, Tunip, Qatna lie beside us).
value.summary: Turn 2, first orders. Niya (Takuwa), vassal of Mitanni, 21 shekels in treasury, army of 750 men at home, walls 1, tax 37%. Envoy c57 is at Mitanni delivering this year's tribute. Holding position; no new letters, levies or works this season.

ledger.entry: Vassal of Mitanni by sealed tablet k61 (turn 0): 10 shekels tribute a year, we take no arms against Mitanni or its friends and our troops come when called; Mitanni protects our land. Turn 1: envoy Akit-Teshup carries 10 shekels of tribute, promised nothing more.

value.notes: Turn 2. Elam is small (Susa, walls 2, army 1750, treasury ~80). Babylonia is the strong neighbour: its armies hold Nippur, Ur, Dur-Kurigalzu and Babili. Plan: stay defensive, keep the army in Susa where it can strike a besieger, and seek peace with Babylonia (envoy Humban-ahpi, oath of non-aggression). Court with Arrapha (Shutatna) to bind a friend on Babylonia's northern flank. Watch Ur and Nippur. Do not spend gold on troops we cannot afford; keep a reserve for the army's pay. If Babylonia refuses peace and moves on Susa, the army holds the walls and asks for help.
value.summary: Opening. Envoys sent: Humban-ahpi (c122) to Babylonia proposing peace and a non-aggression oath; Shutatna (c62) to Arrapha proposing brotherhood. Army holds Susa. Economy: tax 38%, stores 53, purse ~1500. No conquests planned yet.

ledger.entry: Turn 2: envoy Humban-ahpi sent with a proposal of brotherhood and a sealed oath that neither king sends troops into the other's land. Mandate: peace and gifts, no land promised. Babylonia not yet answered.
Turn 2: envoy Shutatna sent with a proposal of brotherhood and a sealed oath of non-aggression. Mandate: peace and gifts, no land promised.

value.notes: Turn 2. Gezer's army (446 men) now stands in Megiddo, next to Akko. Megiddo's own army was destroyed. Akko has walls 1 and one army of 500 men; treasury 36. Keep the army in Akko, avoid wars with Hazor, Tyre and Megiddo, and keep the treasury. Egypt is my protector under the vassal tablet of turn 0 (tribute 5 a year, not yet sent). Do not send c60 or c61 until I can pay their fees (54 and 61 due on completion). If Gezer or Hazor moves against Akko, the army holds within the walls.
value.summary: Turn 1-2: Akko, Egyptian vassal, one army of 500 men in Akko, treasury 36. Gezer's army moved into Megiddo on turn 2, the first sign of hostility nearby. No letters sent yet. Holding position while the treasury is small.

ledger.entry: Vassal tablet of turn 0 (k23): 5 shekels of gold a year as tribute; we take no arms against Egypt or its friends; Egypt protects our land. Tribute not yet sent; no letters sent since. Keep it in good standing when the treasury allows.

value.notes: Plan: Kaska is weak (43rd of 47, treasury 0, one army of 2500 at kaska, no walls). Survive first. Hold the army at kaska (rough ground helps it). Hatti is the only neighbour; our envoy Haamashshi (c15) carries a peace-and-brotherhood proposal (no troops into each other's lands). Do not attack Hatti's Sapinuwa or Samuha: their armies are 1000-3000 men and would destroy ours. Watch troop movements into kaska, samuha, sapinuwa, hattusa. Keep the army fed; sell surplus grain at kaska market only if the treasury needs gold for pay. Once the envoy returns from Hatti, reopen orders.
value.summary: Turn 2. Kaska: army 2500 at kaska, treasury 0, envoy c15 en route to Hatti (arrives ~turn 3) with peace/brotherhood tablet. Strategy: defensive, survive and grow, keep peace with Hatti.

ledger.entry: Turn 1: envoy Haamashshi sent to Hatti proposing brotherhood and peace, neither king to send troops into the other's land; tablet to be sealed by Shamash, Amun, Marduk, Teshub. Nothing sealed yet. Envoy fee 130 (65 paid on done, 65 due).

value.notes: Turn 2. Plan: hold Apasa and the army; no attack. Lukka (3750 men in rough ground) is not worth attacking: our 10000 men count only ~2 units against ~1.75 plus ground, and the gain is small (yield 15). Keep peace with Hatti (brother) and Egypt if possible; seek trade. Vassals Mira and Seha pay 15 a year each; check that tribute arrives. Envoys Mane (to Lukka) and Zitanza (to Hatti) are out; await their reports. Fleet was lost in a storm; rebuild only when treasury allows (fleet costs 120, needs Apasa levy). Keep tolls and tax as they are.
value.summary: Arzawa, Great King, at Apasa. One army of 10000 men at Apasa; no fleet (lost in storm). Treasury 151. Vassals: Mira and Seha (15/yr each). Envoys sent: Mane to Lukka (peace, brotherhood, oath), Zitanza to Hatti (same). Policy: defensive, avoid costly war, build treasury, trade grain via markets.

ledger.entry: Sent Mane (turn 1) proposing peace and brotherhood, tablet of no-attack. Awaiting reply.
Sent Zitanza (turn 1) proposing peace and brotherhood, tablet of no-attack. Hatti already calls us brother.
Vassal: owes 15 shekels a year tribute to Arzawa; protection clause.
Vassal: owes 15 shekels a year tribute to Arzawa; protection clause.

value.notes: Plan: Ugarit is small (yield 40, 75 shekels, army 2000, fleet 2000). Egypt is my overlord by vassal tablet k1 (20 shekels tribute a year, I owe troops when called and protection of my land). Alalakh is a peace-minded neighbour: brotherhood oath sent via Arih-hamanna (tablet: neither sends troops into the other's land). Debt d4 of 55 to Arih-hamanna due turn 7: repay by turn 6 if treasury allows. Keep army and fleet at home; do not attack Alalakh (General's advice rejected: it breaks my oath). Watch Niya, Tunip, Sumur (Egypt's). Feed the town from stores since the market is empty.
value.summary: Turn 2, first orders. Ugarit, vassal of Egypt (tribute 20/yr). Envoys: Ilimilku to Egypt with tribute; Arih-hamanna to Alalakh proposing a non-aggression brotherhood tablet. Debt 55 to Arih-hamanna by turn 7. Holding at home.

ledger.entry: Vassal of Egypt by tablet k1: 20 shekels tribute yearly, my troops to come when called, my land under Egypt's protection. Turn 1: Ilimilku carries this year's tribute (20 shekels).

Turn 1: Arih-hamanna carries proposal of brotherhood: neither to send troops into the other's lands; tablet to seal before the gods. Alalakh is greeted as brother. Arih-hamanna also holds my debt d4 (55 shekels, due turn 7).

orders.letter: Burna-Buriash greets the Pharaoh as brother. Egypt owes Karduniash sixty shekels by the tablet you sealed; we ask that it be repaid now, as is fitting between brothers.
orders.mandate: Collect the debt of 60 shekels on the tablet d2. Accept repayment in gold; promise nothing else.

value.notes: Turn 2 plan: hold the realm. Armies: durkurigalzu (Amanappa), nippur (Addaya moved in), suhu, ur all hold. Threats: Assyria (ashur, ekallate) to the north-east, Elam (peace sealed turn 2), Mitanni and Suteans courted by envoys sent turn 1 (Shagarakti to Mitanni, Ehli-Teshub to Suteans). Egypt owes 60 (tablet d2, due turn 4): Shindishugab (c50) sent to collect. Keep gold for troops and envoys; no war until Assyria's intentions are clearer. Watch Ekallate; General wants to strike it, Steward and Tjaty say wait. Do not strike without a clear gain.
value.summary: Opening. Babylonia rich (1093 shekels, land 837/season). Peace with Elam sealed. Envoys out to Mitanni (vassal tablet offer) and Suteans. Holding positions; collecting Egyptian debt of 60.

ledger.entry: Turn 2: sealed peace (no troops into each other's lands) and fugitives clause, by envoy Humban-ahpi (c122). Elam promised to report a gift exchange; nothing promised by us.
Turn 2: holds debt tablet d2 (Egypt owes 60, due turn 4). Envoy Shindishugab (c50) sent to collect it.

value.notes: Beirut is a small vassal of Egypt (tribute 5 shekels a year, tablet k55). Byblos, Sidon and Damascus border us; their armies are small or modest. Keep the army at home and hold. Envoy Abdi-Baalu (c117) is carrying the tribute to Egypt. Sell surplus grain at our empty market to build the treasury, keeping enough for the town's need of 8 a season. Watch the neighbours for any move on Beirut; if Damascus or Sidon moves, answer with the army inside our walls.
value.summary: Turn 2. Small vassal of Egypt in Beirut with 500 men, walls 1, treasury near 11. Neighbours Byblos, Sidon, Damascus hold small armies. Plan: hold, sell grain for gold, pay tribute on time, keep the vassal tie with Egypt.

ledger.entry: Vassal of Egypt by tablet k55 (turn 0): 5 shekels tribute a year, protection and service. Turn 1: tribute of 5 shekels sent by Abdi-Baalu (c117), due back about turn 3. Nothing broken.

value.notes: Turn 2. Megiddo has no army of its own; the Gezer army (about 446 men) stands inside our walls, and our walls are 1 with no garrison. Gezer is Egypt's vassal. Priorities: (1) keep the capital from falling (a siege here ends the kingdom); (2) rebuild an army once the city is empty of foreign troops (raise_army needs an empty homeland province); (3) use Egypt, Shechem and the Egyptian tribute tablet to press Gezer's overlord to restrain Gezer. Tagi (c58) is on the road to Egypt with 10 shekels of tribute; he carries a mandate to deliver it and promise nothing more. Treasury is only 26 shekels, so avoid gold spending except for essentials. Shechem (Labaya) has sworn brotherhood and no troops into each other's lands; its army of 300 at Shechem is a possible ally against Gezer, but the oath bars sending our troops into Shechem and vice versa.
value.summary: Turn 2: Magidda (Megiddo) lost its army to Gezer's raid; Gezer's army is inside Megiddo's walls (walls 1). Treasury 26. Tagi is en route to Egypt with tribute. Sworn peace with Shechem (no troops into each other's lands). Tax 37%. Plan: hold, raise an army once the city is clear of foreign troops, seek Egyptian protection under the vassal tablet.

ledger.entry: Vassal tablet (turn 0): we pay 10 shekels tribute a year and Egypt protects our land. Turn 1: Tagi sent with 10 shekels tribute, still on the road (due about turn 3). Expect Egypt to be asked to restrain Gezer, its own vassal.
Turn 2: sealed brotherhood tablet: neither king sends troops into the other's lands; fugitives clause. Gift exchange was to follow, not yet paid.

value.notes: Turn 2. Position: Mitanni holds Harran, Washukanni (walls 3), Taidu. Armies: Harran (Asali, loyal so far), Taidu (Artatama, a rival claimant to the Hurrian throne with Hittite backing; watch him closely, he may turn), Washukanni (uncommanded). Peace with Isuwa (no troops across borders), Egypt repaid 200 (Egypt is a friend; debt tablet d1 now settled, tablet to be returned). Babylon demanded vassalage; refused; wants peace. Assyria is a claimant to Great King; Piyamaradu en route for brotherhood. Carchemish, Nuhashshe, Arrapha, Alalakh, Aleppo, Terqa, Niya are vassals. Plan: hold the line, keep grain moving to markets that pay (Dur-Kurigalzu caravans were profitable), watch Artatama. Watch Babylonia for attack. Do not attack Isuwa while the peace stands.
value.summary: Opening season. Mitanni is the fifth-richest realm. Defensive posture: Washukanni army supports Taidu; Harran and Taidu armies hold. Peace sealed with Isuwa; Egypt repaid its debt; Babylon refused vassalage. Watch Artatama in Taidu (rival claimant) and Babylonia's demands.

ledger.entry: Turn 2: Egypt's envoy Ay repaid the 200 shekel debt to Mitanni's house (gold weighed, 200). Friendly. Debt tablet d1 to be returned to Egypt's envoy; brotherhood and peace affirmed.
Turn 2: Babylonia demanded vassalage (60/yr). Refused; proposed peace and no attack. No tablet sealed.
Turn 2: Sealed a peace tablet: neither king sends troops into the other's land; fugitives clause. Tribute demand from my envoy Akip-tasenni (15/yr) is still on the road; not yet agreed.
Turn 2: Vassal by tablet (10/yr) received; protection affirmed.
Turn 2: Vassal tribute of 15 received; my wishes sent.
Turn 2: Vassal by tablet (20/yr). Protection affirmed; no new obligation.

value.notes: Turn 2. Our only army (446 men) stands inside Megiddo's walls (walls 1); Megiddo's field army was destroyed. Plan: besiege Megiddo to wear it down (about 3 seasons at walls 1) and absorb it. Risk: Megiddo is Egypt's vassal and our tablet with Egypt forbids arms against Egypt's friends. Expect Egypt to complain; answer with a letter via Yapahu's successor or a fresh envoy once Yapahu returns (c67 due turn 3). Treasury is tiny (5 shekels). Sell some grain at Gezer to raise gold; town needs 8 a season from its market. Keep the army fed from our stores where possible.
value.summary: Gezer, a small vassal of Egypt (tribute 5 a year). Turn 2: army at Megiddo besieging it. Envoy Yapahu (c67) to Egypt, due back turn 3. Treasury very low.

ledger.entry: Vassal of Egypt by sealed tablet (turn 0): 5 shekels tribute a year, no arms against Egypt or its friends, troops to come when called, Egypt to protect our land. Turn 1 tribute of 5 sent with Yapahu (c67). Turn 2: our army attacked and drove out Megiddo's army (Egypt's vassal) and is now besieging Megiddo. This breaks the spirit of our oath; expect a complaint, answer with a letter.

value.notes: Turn 2. Babylonian army now at suhu, next to terqa. Our only army (1500 men) holds terqa (walls 1). Mitanni is overlord (vassal tablet k47, 15/yr tribute). Hold, keep paying and feeding troops, watch suhu and the Suteans in steppe. Do not start wars; gold is thin (108).
value.summary: Turn 1-2: Hana (Terqa), vassal of Mitanni, holds Terqa with 1500 men. Babylonian army moved to suhu, adjacent. Plan: hold, keep troops paid and fed, stay in Mitanni's good graces, build gold slowly.

ledger.entry: Overlord. Sealed vassal tablet (turn 0): Terqa pays 15 shekels tribute a year; Mitanni protects Terqa. No payments made yet.

value.notes: Aijalon is a tiny vassal of Egypt (tablet k35: 5 shekels tribute a year, troops to answer calls, Egypt protects our land). Treasury 27. Army of 250 holds at home; the Steward and Tjaty both advise holding. Do not spend gold on envoys or jobs yet. Watch Gezer and Gath neighbours; Gath army (500) and Shechem and Jerusalem are nearby. Revisit when the tribute falls due or a neighbour looks weak. Mahu (c22) costs 144 for a job; not affordable now.
value.summary: Turn 2. Hold at home. Minimal spending. Egypt is overlord by vassal tablet; tribute 5 a year. Mahu (c22) available for hire later.

ledger.entry: Vassal to Egypt by sealed tablet (k35, turn 0): 5 shekels tribute a year; we serve their calls to arms. No tribute sent yet.

value.notes: Turn 2. Babylonia's army (1500) stands in Suhu, next to Ashur and Ekallate. Ashur holds 2000 men with walls 3; Nineveh (1000) supports it under standing order s1. Holding everything this season: no attack on Taidu or Arrapha while Babylonia sits beside us. Mitanni brotherhood tablet sealed (no troops across each other's border). Reconsider the General's Suhu strike only if Babylonia's army weakens or stays isolated. Keep granaries; tax goes in as normal.

ledger.entry: Turn 2: sealed brotherhood tablet with Tushratta: neither king sends troops into the other's land; fugitives clause in the tablet. Gift exchange between the courts suggested, not yet sent.

model.text: O king of Isuwa, I hear your words and will carry them faithfully to my lord Tushratta. Your answer is that Isuwa is free, will not serve or pay tribute, and offers peace between our houses if Mitanni keeps its troops from your land. My commission allows me to seal the tablet only as it stands, and I have no power to add terms of land or gold. I will not press you to seal what your scribes cannot read, and I ask only that you give me your answer in writing so that my lord may judge it.

When it is read, I ask that you seal it before Shamash and the gods of your land, so that my lord may know the peace was made in truth.

model.text: Thus I answer for my lord Naphurureya, King of Egypt: "Brother Tushratta, your words have reached my ears and I carry them home gladly. Let the brotherhood between our houses stand as it stood in the days of our fathers, and let there be peace between Egypt and Mitanni forever. Now, my lord asks that the tablet be returned into my hand, that the account between us be closed and nothing remain to trouble our friendship. May it be well with you, your house, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country."
